## Definition

Use the nonlinear program and SQP subproblem conventions of
[[def-sqp-linearized-quadratic-subproblem]]. For $\rho>0$, define the
nondifferentiable L1 merit function
$$\psi_\rho(x)=f(x)+\rho\left(\|h(x)\|_1+\|[g(x)]_+\|_1\right).$$
For a subproblem step $p$ at $x$, its linearized predicted decrease is
$$D_\rho(x,p)=-\left[\nabla f(x)^Tp+\rho\left(\|h(x)+Dh(x)p\|_1-\|h(x)\|_1+ \|[g(x)+Dg(x)p]_+\|_1-\|[g(x)]_+\|_1\right)\right].$$
A trial fraction $t\in(0,1]$ satisfies the Armijo test with coefficient
$\sigma\in(0,1)$ when
$$\psi_\rho(x+tp)\le\psi_\rho(x)-\sigma tD_\rho(x,p).$$
The definition alone does not assert $D_\rho(x,p)>0$, existence of an
accepted fraction, or convergence of a sequence of accepted SQP steps.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The smooth program and a subproblem displacement $p$, with penalty
parameter $\rho>0$.

[F1] [[def-sqp-linearized-quadratic-subproblem]] defines the affine
linearized equality and inequality residuals and uses $g\le0$.

[A1] The penalty is $\rho>0$, the point $x$ belongs to $U$, and the trial
point belongs to $U$ whenever its nonlinear merit is evaluated.

## Proof

1.1 The norm and positive-part terms in $\psi_\rho$ are finite for every $x\in U$, since the constraint maps are real-valued and the dimensions are finite. The displayed $D_\rho(x,p)$ is therefore the negative of the change in the linear objective-plus-penalty model from displacement $0$ to $p$. [given, A1, F1, algebra]

2.1 Replacing $p$ by $tp$ in that same model gives a distinct finite trial value; the Armijo inequality compares it with the actual nonlinear merit at $x+tp$. This definition supplies a test only and, as stated, implies no positivity or acceptance claim. [given, A1, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

      url: https://www.ime.unicamp.br/~pulino/MT404/TextosOnline/NocedalJ.pdf
      locator: "Chapter 17 §17.4, printed pp. 511–521 / PDF pp. 529–539."
    - title: "Dimitri P. Bertsekas, Constrained Optimization and Lagrange Multiplier Methods"
      url: https://www.mit.edu/~dimitrib/Constrained-Opt.pdf
      locator: "Chapter 2 §2.2, printed pp. 104–121."
---

## Definition

Fix a smooth program as in
[[def-sqp-augmented-lagrangian-equality-and-inequality]], a penalty
$\rho>0$, finite outer cap $K\ge1$, finite per-call inner cap $M\ge1$,
tolerances $\epsilon_k\ge0$, and KKT tolerance $\tau\ge0$. A supplied
finite-budget inner procedure receives
$(x_k,\nu_k,\lambda_k,\rho,\epsilon_k,M)$, performs at most $M$ inner
iterations, and returns one of: `success(x_k^+,\widehat\epsilon_k)` with
$x_k^+\in U$ and
$\widehat\epsilon_k=\|\nabla_x\mathcal L_\rho(x_k^+,\nu_k,\lambda_k)\|_2
\le\epsilon_k$; `budget-exhausted(x_{\rm last},\widehat\epsilon_{\rm last})`
with $x_{\rm last}\in U$ and
$\widehat\epsilon_{\rm last}=
\|\nabla_x\mathcal L_\rho(x_{\rm last},\nu_k,\lambda_k)\|_2$; or
`failure(data)` when it cannot continue or report a residual. Each inner
iteration and report computation is finite, and the procedure returns by its
cap.

Initialize $x_0\in U$, $\nu_0\in\mathbb R^p$, and
$\lambda_0\in\mathbb R^m_+$. For $k=0,\ldots,K-1$:

1. Call the inner procedure with cap $M$. On
   `budget-exhausted(x_{\rm last},\widehat\epsilon_{\rm last})`, return
   `inner-budget-exhausted` with current $(x_k,\nu_k,\lambda_k)$, that point,
   and residual. On `failure(data)`,
   return `inner-failure` with the data. If a purported success reports a
   residual exceeding $\epsilon_k$, return `inner-failure` with the reported
   data. Otherwise store its reported inner residual
   $\widehat\epsilon_k$.
2. Set
   $$\nu_{k+1}=\nu_k+\rho h(x_k^+),\qquad \lambda_{k+1}=[\lambda_k+\rho g(x_k^+)]_+.$$
3. Set $r_k=r_{\rm KKT}(x_k^+,\nu_{k+1},\lambda_{k+1})$. If $r_k\le\tau$,
   return `kkt-tolerance-reached` with $x_k^+$, $(\nu_{k+1},\lambda_{k+1})$,
   $r_k$, and $\widehat\epsilon_k$; otherwise set $x_{k+1}=x_k^+$ and
   continue.

If all $K$ outer iterations finish without that test passing, return
`outer-budget-exhausted` with $x_K$, $(\nu_K,\lambda_K)$, the last KKT
residual $r_{K-1}$, and inner residual $\widehat\epsilon_{K-1}$. The routine
claims neither convergence nor that the inner procedure succeeds within its
cap.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The finite caps and tolerances, the smooth program, and the
nonnegative initial inequality multiplier.

[F1] [[def-sqp-augmented-lagrangian-equality-and-inequality]] defines the
projected inequality augmented Lagrangian and updates
$\nu^+=\nu+\rho h(x^+)$, $\lambda^+=[\lambda+\rho g(x^+)]_+$.

[F2] [[def-kkt-residual-and-normal-cone]] defines the KKT residual as a sum
of stationarity, primal feasibility, dual feasibility and complementarity
residual norms.

[A1] The initial multiplier has $\lambda_0\ge0$, the penalty is positive,
and the inner and outer caps are positive finite integers. The supplied
inner procedure obeys its cap and returns the stated residual or failure
data.

## Proof

1.1 The initialization gives $\lambda_0\ge0$; each projection in [F1] again has nonnegative components, so every multiplier iterate is in the declared domain. A successful inner-procedure return is checked against the declared inner residual tolerance before any update uses it. [given, A1, F1, algebra]

2.1 Each outer iteration performs at most $M$ inner iterations, one finite multiplier update, and one residual test from [F2]. Thus it either returns one of the stated inner statuses at that iteration or advances the integer index; the cap $K$ forces a return after at most $KM$ inner iterations and $K$ outer tests. If the outer cap is reached, the last reported inner and KKT residuals are returned. The residual test only certifies its displayed tolerance and does not itself assert that the algorithm reaches it. [given, A1, F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra] ∎
items/lem-sqp-convex-quadratic-subproble:
---
id: lem-sqp-convex-quadratic-subproblem-has-unique-kkt-certificate
kind: lemma
title: "A feasible strictly convex linear-constrained QP has a unique KKT minimizer with independent active support"
status: draft
origin: pipeline
pipeline_run: numerical-optimization-dynamics-2026-10-16
dependency_level: 3
deps:
  - def-sqp-linearized-quadratic-subproblem
  - thm-farkas-alternative-for-finite-linear-systems
  - thm-convex-kkt-sufficiency-and-normal-cone-certificate
  - thm-heine-borel-rn
  - thm-extreme-value-metric
  - def-euclidean-inner-product
  - thm-cauchy-schwarz-and-the-euclidean-norm
proof_strategy: direct
provenance:
  statement: ai-altered
  proof: ai-altered
verification:
  precheck: pending
sources:
  references:
    - title: "Jorge Nocedal and Stephen J. Wright, Numerical Optimization, 2nd ed."
      url: https://www.ime.unicamp.br/~pulino/MT404/TextosOnline/NocedalJ.pdf
      locator: "Chapter 16 §§16.1–16.4, printed pp. 451–465 / PDF pp. 469–483; convex QP KKT and active-set support."
---

## Statement

Let $q(p)=c^Tp+\tfrac12p^TBp$ on $\mathbb R^n$, where $B=B^T$ is positive
definite. Let the feasible set be the nonempty polyhedron
$$C=\{p:Ap=b,\ G_ip+d_i\le0\ (1\le i\le m)\},$$
where the equality rows of $A$ are linearly independent (zero rows are
allowed). Then $q$ has a unique minimizer $p_*$. There are equality
multipliers $\nu$ and inequality multipliers $\lambda_i\ge0$ such that
$$Bp_*+c+A^T\nu+\sum_i\lambda_iG_i^T=0, \qquad \lambda_i(G_ip_*+d_i)=0.$$
They can be chosen so that the equality rows and the active inequality rows
with $\lambda_i>0$ are linearly independent. This KKT tuple certifies the
global minimizer.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The quadratic objective, the nonempty feasible polyhedron, and the
independent equality-row convention in the Statement.

[A1] $B$ is symmetric positive definite and $C$ is nonempty.

[F1] [[def-sqp-linearized-quadratic-subproblem]]: the SQP subproblem has a
positive-definite quadratic objective and affine equality and inequality
constraints, with inequalities in the $\le0$ convention.

[F2] [[thm-farkas-alternative-for-finite-linear-systems]]: for a matrix $M$
and vector $v$, either $Mz=v$ for some $z\ge0$, or there is $y$ with
$M^Ty\ge0$ and $v^Ty<0$, but not both.

[F3] [[thm-convex-kkt-sufficiency-and-normal-cone-certificate]]: a feasible
KKT tuple for a differentiable convex objective with affine convex
inequalities and affine equalities is a global minimizer.

[F4] [[thm-heine-borel-rn]] and [[thm-extreme-value-metric]]: closed bounded
subsets of $\mathbb R^n$ are compact, and a continuous function on a
nonempty compact metric space attains its minimum.

[F5] [[def-euclidean-inner-product]] defines the Euclidean inner product
$u^Tv$ and norm $\|u\|_2=\sqrt{u^Tu}$.

[F6] [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-and-the-euclidean-norm]]: $|u^Tv|\le\|u\|_2\|v\|_2$.

## Proof

1.1 The unit sphere is compact by [F4]. The continuous function $z\mapsto z^TBz$ is positive on it, so it attains a positive minimum $\alpha$. Thus $q(p)\ge\frac{\alpha}{2}\|p\|_2^2-\|c\|_2\|p\|_2$ by [F6], which tends to $+\infty$ as $\|p\|_2\to\infty$. By [F1], the constraint rows are affine, so their closed half-spaces and affine equality sets intersect in a closed set; choosing one feasible $p_0$, the nonempty sublevel $\{p\in C:q(p)\le q(p_0)\}$ is bounded and closed, hence compact by [F4]. The minimum is attained there and therefore on $C$. [given, F1, F4, F5, F6, algebra, choose]

2.1 If two distinct feasible points $p_1,p_2$ minimized $q$, their midpoint is feasible and $$q\bigl((p_1+p_2)/2\bigr)=\tfrac12q(p_1)+\tfrac12q(p_2)-\tfrac18(p_1-p_2)^TB(p_1-p_2)<q(p_1),$$ contradicting minimality. Hence the minimizer $p_*$ is unique. [step 1.1, given, A1, algebra]

2.2 Let $I=\{i:G_ip_*+d_i=0\}$. For any $z$ with $Az=0$ and $G_iz\le0$ for $i\in I$, inactive constraints have positive slack, so for all sufficiently small $t>0$, $p_*+tz\in C$. Minimality and the one-sided derivative at $t=0$ give $(Bp_*+c)^Tz\ge0$. Therefore $v:=-(Bp_*+c)$ satisfies $v^Tz\le0$ for every such $z$. [given, A1, F1, step 1.1, choose, algebra]

3.1 If $v$ were not representable as $A^T\eta+\sum_{i\in I}\mu_iG_i^T$ with $\mu_i\ge0$, apply [F2] to the matrix whose columns are $G_i^T$ for $i\in I$, the columns of $A^T$, and their negatives, with right-hand side $v$. The alternative gives $y$ with $G_iy\ge0$, $Ay=0$, and $v^Ty<0$. Then $z=-y$ satisfies the direction conditions of step 2.2 but $v^Tz>0$, a contradiction. Thus $v=A^T\eta+\sum_{i\in I}\mu_iG_i^T$ for some $\mu_i\ge0$. Since $v=-(Bp_*+c)$, this is KKT stationarity with equality multiplier $\eta$; setting inactive multipliers to zero gives complementarity. [F2, step 2.2, algebra, assume-contra, discharge-contradiction]

4.1 If $A$ has positive row count, full row rank makes $AA^T$ positive definite, so set $P=I-A^T(AA^T)^{-1}A$; if it has zero rows, set $P=I$. Direct multiplication gives $AP=0$, $P^T=P$, and $P^2=P$, and $Pz=z$ for every $z\in\ker A$. Thus $P$ is the orthogonal projection onto $\ker A$ and $\ker P=\operatorname{range}(A^T)$. Project the multiplier representation from step 3.1. If the projected active normals with positive coefficients are dependent, choose a nonzero dependence, change its sign to give a positive coefficient, and subtract $t$ times that relation, where $t$ is the minimum ratio of a current multiplier to a positive dependence coefficient. All coefficients remain nonnegative and at least one becomes zero. Repeating finitely many times leaves independent projected normals. Their unprojected remainder lies in $\ker P=\operatorname{range}(A^T)$, so it is absorbed into the equality multiplier. If a linear combination of the equality rows and supported active rows is zero, projecting it by $P$ first forces all active coefficients to be zero by projected independence; full row rank then forces the equality coefficients to be zero. [A1, step 3.1, given, algebra, construct, induction]

5.1 The feasible tuple from steps 3.1–3.1 satisfies the hypotheses of [F3], because $q$ is differentiable and convex and every constraint is affine. Thus it certifies a global minimizer; step 2.1 makes that global minimizer unique. [F3, step 2.1, step 3.1] ∎

id: alg-sqp-exhaustive-active-set-qp-solve
kind: algorithm
title: "Exact exhaustive active-set solve for the SQP quadratic subproblem"
status: draft
origin: pipeline
pipeline_run: numerical-optimization-dynamics-2026-10-16
dependency_level: 3
deps:
  - def-sqp-linearized-quadratic-subproblem
  - lem-sqp-kkt-matrix-nonsingularity-under-reduced-curvature
proof_strategy: direct
provenance:

  proof: ai-altered
verification:

sources:
  references:
    - title: "Jorge Nocedal and Stephen J. Wright, Numerical Optimization, 2nd ed."
      url: https://www.ime.unicamp.br/~pulino/MT404/TextosOnline/NocedalJ.pdf
      locator: "Chapter 16 §§16.1–16.4, printed pp. 451–465 / PDF pp. 469–483; KKT systems for convex QPs and active sets."
---

## Definition

Input an SQP subproblem from [[def-sqp-linearized-quadratic-subproblem]],
using exact real arithmetic. First reduce the linearized equality system
$A_Ep=b_E$: test consistency, and, if consistent, retain the
lexicographically first maximal independent set $E$ of equality row indices
with their right-hand sides. If it is inconsistent, return
`QP-infeasible`.

For each subset $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}$ in increasing bit-mask order:

1. Stack the retained equality rows and the inequality rows $G_i$ for $i\in J$.
   If these rows are dependent, skip $J$.
2. Treat the selected inequalities as equalities $G_ip=-d_i$ and solve
   $$\begin{bmatrix}B&A_J^T\\A_J&0\end{bmatrix} \binom{p}{\eta}=\binom{-c}{b_J},$$
   where $c=\nabla f(x)$, $A_J$ is the stacked matrix with equality rows $E$
   followed by selected inequality rows $J$, and $b_J$ is the right-hand side
   in that same row order. The multiplier vector $\eta$ is stored in this row
   order. The KKT matrix is
   nonsingular by [[lem-sqp-kkt-matrix-nonsingularity-under-reduced-curvature]].
3. Discard the candidate if any linearized inequality is violated or any
   selected inequality multiplier is negative. Otherwise store $(p,\eta,J)$.

If no candidate is stored, return `QP-infeasible`. Otherwise return the
stored candidate with least quadratic objective, breaking an exact tie by the
least subset bit mask, as `solution(p, nu, lambda, E, J)`. Here $\nu$ is
the full equality-multiplier vector, initialized to zero and filled from the
equality components of $\eta$ at indices $E$; $\lambda$ is the full
inequality-multiplier vector, initialized to zero and filled from the selected
components at indices $J$. A finite-precision
implementation that cannot complete a rank test or solve must return
`numerical-failure`; this definition's exact-arithmetic branch has no such
failure. The loop tests at most $2^m$ inequality subsets. It requires no
feasible initial step and specifies no pivoting rule for an iterative working
set solver.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** An affine-constraint quadratic subproblem with $B\succ0$ and
exact real arithmetic.

[F1] [[def-sqp-linearized-quadratic-subproblem]] defines the quadratic
objective and affine feasible set.

[F2] [[lem-sqp-kkt-matrix-nonsingularity-under-reduced-curvature]] states
that the KKT block matrix is nonsingular when its constraint rows are
independent and the Hessian is positive definite on their null space.

[A1] The quadratic matrix $B$ is symmetric positive definite and all rank,
consistency, solve, and comparison operations use exact real arithmetic.

## Proof

1.1 The equality reduction and subset enumeration each examine finitely many row subsets. Every retained equality system is equivalent to the original consistent system, and every selected subset passing the rank test has a nonsingular KKT matrix by [F2], because $B\succ0$ on every subspace. Thus each candidate solve is uniquely defined. [given, A1, F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 Each accepted candidate is checked against all inequalities and has nonnegative selected inequality multipliers. The returned full vectors $(\nu,\lambda)$ are the reduced KKT multipliers placed at their original indices and zero elsewhere, so they give the same stationarity equation; feasibility of the retained equality system is equivalent to feasibility of the original consistent system. Thus the return is a feasible KKT tuple for the full QP. If none is accepted, the routine returns its specified infeasibility status. The exact meaning of that status is a separate theorem claim. [given, A1, F1, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

id: alg-sqp-feasible-working-set-qp-solve
kind: algorithm
title: "Feasible active-set QP solve with blocking constraints and a finite cap"
status: draft
origin: pipeline
pipeline_run: numerical-optimization-dynamics-2026-10-16
dependency_level: 3
deps:
  - def-sqp-linearized-quadratic-subproblem
  - lem-sqp-kkt-matrix-nonsingularity-under-reduced-curvature

sources:
  references:
    - title: "Jorge Nocedal and Stephen J. Wright, Numerical Optimization, 2nd ed."
      url: https://www.ime.unicamp.br/~pulino/MT404/TextosOnline/NocedalJ.pdf
      locator: "Chapter 16 §16.4, Algorithm 16.1 and finite-termination discussion, printed pp. 455–465 / PDF pp. 475–484."
---

## Definition

Input a strictly convex quadratic program
$$q(z)=\tfrac12z^TBz+c^Tz,\qquad Az=b,\qquad G_iz+d_i\le0\ (1\le i\le m),$$
with $B=B^T\succ0$, a feasible starting point $z_0$, a working set
$W_0$ of active inequality indices whose rows together with the equality
rows are independent, and a finite iteration cap $N\ge1$. Fix ties by least
index. For each iteration $k=0,\ldots,N-1$:

1. Solve the equality-constrained direction problem
   $$\min_u\quad (Bz_k+c)^Tu+\tfrac12u^TBu \quad\text{subject to}\quad Au=0,\quad G_iu=0\ (i\in W_k).$$
   Its KKT matrix is nonsingular by
   [[lem-sqp-kkt-matrix-nonsingularity-under-reduced-curvature]]. If the
   linear solve fails, return `numerical-failure`.
2. If $u=0$, inspect the inequality multipliers $\mu_i$ for $i\in W_k$.
   If every $\mu_i\ge0$, return `solution(z_k, multipliers, W_k)`. Otherwise
   delete the least-index $j\in W_k$ with $\mu_j<0$ and continue at the same
   feasible point with the reduced working set.
3. If $u\ne0$, for every $i\notin W_k$ with $G_iu>0$ compute
   $$\alpha_i=-\frac{G_iz_k+d_i}{G_iu},\qquad \alpha_k=\min\bigl(1,\min_{i\notin W_k,\ G_iu>0}\alpha_i\bigr),$$
   using $\alpha_k=1$ when there is no such index. If $\alpha_k=0$, return
   `degenerate-block`. Otherwise set $z_{k+1}=z_k+\alpha_ku$. If
   $\alpha_k<1$, add the least-index blocker attaining $\alpha_k$ to $W_k$;
   if adding it makes the rows dependent, return `dependent-blocker`. If
   $\alpha_k=1$, the new point minimizes $q$ on the current working-set
   face, even if an unselected inequality becomes active at the endpoint. Set
   all those unselected multipliers to zero, and return if the current
   inequality multipliers are nonnegative; otherwise delete the least-index
   negative-multiplier constraint before continuing.

If the cap is reached first, return `iteration-budget-exhausted` with the
last feasible iterate and multipliers. Every returned non-solution status is
inconclusive about optimality. The algorithm does not silently add a
zero-length blocking step.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A feasible starting point, independent initial working rows,
$B\succ0$, and a positive finite iteration cap.

[F1] [[def-sqp-linearized-quadratic-subproblem]] fixes the $\le0$
constraint convention and quadratic objective.

[F2] [[lem-sqp-kkt-matrix-nonsingularity-under-reduced-curvature]] makes
each stated working-face KKT system uniquely solvable.

[A1] The starting point is feasible, $B$ is symmetric positive definite,
the initial working rows are independent, and $N$ is a positive integer.

## Proof

1.1 The direction problem has Hessian $B\succ0$ on the null space of the working rows, and those rows are independent by the input condition and the dependent-blocker guard. Hence [F2] applies. If $G_i u>0$, feasibility of $z_k$ gives $\alpha_i\ge0$, and taking the minimum blocking fraction keeps every linear inequality feasible along $z_k+t u$ for $0\le t\le\alpha_k$. [given, F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 Deleting a row leaves the iterate feasible; adding an independent blocking row preserves independent working rows; a zero blocking step or failed solve exits explicitly. Since at most $N$ direction solves are attempted, the procedure returns a listed solution status or a listed inconclusive status after finitely many iterations. [given, A1, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

      locator: "Chapter 18 §§18.8 and 18.11, printed pp. 556–558 and 568–569 / PDF pp. 574–576 and 586–587; second-order correction formula and line-search use."
---

## Definition

Let $c_A:U\to\mathbb R^r$ collect the equality constraints and a specified
set of active inequality constraints, in that order. Given $x,x+p\in U$,
assume $A=Dc_A(x)$ has full row rank and the SQP step satisfies
$c_A(x)+Ap=0$. For $r>0$, compute
$$w=-A^T(AA^T)^{-1}c_A(x+p)$$
and return $p+w$ as the corrected displacement. If the rank test fails,
the inverse or evaluation fails, return `correction-failure`. If $r=0$,
return $p$ with $w=0$. This is a correction for the specified active
constraints; it does not certify feasibility of inactive constraints.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A linearized SQP step and the active constraint map $c_A$ at a
point where the trial evaluations are defined.

[F1] [[def-sqp-linearized-quadratic-subproblem]] defines the affine
linearized constraints and the equation $c_A(x)+Dc_A(x)p=0$ on a chosen
active set.

[A1] The selected active constraint Jacobian $A=Dc_A(x)$ has full row rank,
and the trial points $x$ and $x+p$ lie in $U$.

## Proof

1.1 Full row rank implies that for every nonzero $v\in\mathbb R^r$, $v^TAA^Tv=\|A^Tv\|_2^2>0$; hence $AA^T$ is invertible. The formula is therefore defined and satisfies $Aw=-c_A(x+p)$. [given, F1, algebra]

2.1 If $u$ is any other correction satisfying $Au=-c_A(x+p)$, then $u-w\in\ker A$, while $w\in\operatorname{range}(A^T)$. The inclusion $\operatorname{range}(A^T)\subseteq(\ker A)^\perp$ follows from $\langle A^Tv,z\rangle=\langle v,Az\rangle=0$; both spaces have dimension $\operatorname{rank}A$, so they are equal. Therefore $\|u\|_2^2=\|w\|_2^2+\|u-w\|_2^2\ge\|w\|_2^2$, with equality only for $u=w$. For $r=0$, the unique minimum-norm correction is zero. [given, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

## Definition

Let $c_A(x)=(h(x),g_I(x))$ stack all equalities and the identified active
inequalities, and let $\mu=(\nu,\lambda_I)$. For a current pair $(x,\mu)$,
form
$$F_A(x,\mu)=\binom{\nabla_x L(x,\nu,\lambda_I,0_{I^c})}{c_A(x)},\qquad J_A(x,\mu)=\begin{bmatrix}\nabla^2_{xx}L(x,\nu,\lambda_I,0_{I^c})&Dc_A(x)^T\\Dc_A(x)&0\end{bmatrix}.$$
If $J_A$ is nonsingular, solve
$$J_A\binom{p}{\delta\mu}=-F_A(x,\mu)$$
and return the full Newton pair $(x+p,\mu+\delta\mu)$. A failed rank test
or solve returns `kkt-solve-failure`. The active set is supplied to this
step; this algorithm has no line search and makes no global convergence
claim.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The program convention of
[[def-inequality-constrained-program-and-kkt-geometry]], an identified
active set $I$, and a current primal-dual pair.

[F1] [[def-sqp-linearized-quadratic-subproblem]] uses the Lagrangian
Hessian in the quadratic model and linearizes the constraints.

[F2] [[lem-sqp-kkt-matrix-nonsingularity-under-reduced-curvature]] gives
the nonsingularity criterion for the displayed saddle-point matrix.

[F3] [[def-inequality-constrained-program-and-kkt-geometry]] fixes the
active-set Lagrangian $L=f+\nu^Th+\lambda^Tg$ and the nonnegative
inequality-multiplier convention.

[A1] The active set is identified, the active rows are independent, and
the exact Lagrangian Hessian is positive on their null space whenever a
step is claimed.

## Proof

1.1 Differentiating $F_A$ with respect to $(x,\mu)$ gives the block matrix $J_A$: the derivative of stationarity in $x$ is the exact Lagrangian Hessian, its derivative in $\mu$ is $Dc_A(x)^T$, and the derivative of the constraint block is $Dc_A(x)$. Thus the linear solve is precisely the Newton equation for $F_A=0$. [given, F1, F3, algebra]

2.1 When the active rows are independent and the Lagrangian Hessian is positive on their null space, [F2] makes that Newton equation uniquely solvable. Otherwise the algorithm reports failure and does not return a Newton step; a returned pair is the stated full step. [given, A1, F2, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

## Definition

Let $c_A(x)$ stack the equality and identified active constraints, and let
$A=Dc_A(x)$ have full row rank. Set
$$P=I-A^T(AA^T)^{-1}A$$
when $A$ has positive row count and $P=I$ when it has zero rows. Given the
exact Lagrangian Hessian $H$ and a symmetric positive-definite full-memory
BFGS matrix $B$, define
$$H_{\rm red}=H+P(B-H)P.$$
Solve the active KKT system with $H_{\rm red}$ in its upper-left block and
right-hand side $-F_A(x,\mu)$ as in
[[alg-sqp-exact-hessian-newton-step]]. If the rows are dependent or the
solve fails, return `kkt-solve-failure`.

For a curvature pair $(s,y)$ with $s^Ty>0$, the optional next-model update
is
$$B^+=B-\frac{(Bs)(Bs)^T}{s^TBs}+\frac{yy^T}{s^Ty};$$
if $s^Ty\le0$, skip the update and retain $B$. The curvature pair is defined
as in [[def-bfgs-curvature-pair-and-update-formulas]].

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** An identified active set with independent rows, its SQP KKT
residual $F_A$, exact Lagrangian Hessian $H$, and $B\succ0$.

[F1] [[def-sqp-linearized-quadratic-subproblem]] fixes the active-row
KKT block convention.

[F2] [[lem-sqp-kkt-matrix-nonsingularity-under-reduced-curvature]] states
that reduced positive curvature and independent rows imply nonsingularity.

[F3] [[def-bfgs-curvature-pair-and-update-formulas]] defines the BFGS
curvature pair and update.

[F4] [[lem-bfgs-updates-preserve-secant-symmetry-and-spd]]: if $B\succ0$
and $s^Ty>0$, the BFGS update is symmetric positive definite.

[F5] [[def-inequality-constrained-program-and-kkt-geometry]] fixes the
active set and the Lagrangian multiplier convention used in $F_A$.

[A1] The current active rows are independent, and the supplied BFGS model
is symmetric positive definite.

## Proof

1.1 Full row rank gives $AP=0$, $P^T=P$, and $Pz=z$ for $z\in\ker A$; these follow by multiplying out the displayed projector. Hence for every $z\in\ker A$, $z^TH_{\rm red}z=z^TBz>0$. Applying [F2] to $H_{\rm red}$ shows that the KKT solve is nonsingular. [given, F1, F2, F5, algebra]

2.1 If $s^Ty>0$, the update in [F3] is symmetric and remains positive definite by [F4]. If $s^Ty\le0$, the algorithm retains the already positive-definite $B$. Thus every successful model update preserves the stated $B\succ0$ invariant. [given, F3, F4, step 1.1] ∎

## Definition

At $x\in U$, choose a positive-definite SQP model matrix and solve the exact
quadratic subproblem by
[[alg-sqp-exhaustive-active-set-qp-solve]]. If it reports infeasibility or
failure, return that status. On a solution return, retain its step $p$, full
QP multiplier vectors $(\nu^{QP},\lambda^{QP})$, retained equality basis
$E$, and selected inequality support $J$. The stacked rows $Dh_E(x)$ and
$Dg_J(x)$ are independent, and the selected rows satisfy
$h_E(x)+Dh_E(x)p=0$ and $g_J(x)+Dg_J(x)p=0$. Given parameters $\rho_0>0$,
$\gamma>1$, $\beta\in(0,1)$, $\sigma\in(0,1)$ and finite integer caps
$R,J_{\max}\ge1$, keep the resulting step $p$ fixed, initialize flags
$P_{\rm pos}=\mathrm{false}$ and $P_{\rm dom}=\mathrm{false}$, and perform
attempts $r=0,\ldots,R-1$ with $\rho_r=\rho_0\gamma^r$:

1. Compute $D_r=D_{\rho_r}(x,p)$ from
   [[def-sqp-l1-exact-penalty-merit]]. If $D_r\le0$, go to the next penalty.
   Otherwise set $P_{\rm pos}=\mathrm{true}$.
2. If $x+p\in U$, call
   [[alg-sqp-second-order-correction]] with the specified map
   $c_A=(h_E,g_J)$. If it returns a correction $w$ and $x+p+w\in U$, set
   $P_{\rm dom}=\mathrm{true}$ and test
   $\psi_{\rho_r}(x+p+w)\le\psi_{\rho_r}(x)-\sigma D_r$. If it passes,
   return `accepted-soc` with $x+p+w$, $p$, $(\nu^{QP},\lambda^{QP})$, $E$,
   and $J$. If $x+p\notin U$, skip the correction call.
3. For $j=0,\ldots,J_{\max}-1$, set $t_j=\beta^j$. Whenever $x+t_jp\in U$,
   set $P_{\rm dom}=\mathrm{true}$ and test
   $$\psi_{\rho_r}(x+t_jp)\le\psi_{\rho_r}(x)-\sigma t_jD_r.$$
   On the first passing test, return `accepted` with $x+t_jp$, $t_j$,
   $p$, $(\nu^{QP},\lambda^{QP})$, $E$, and $J$.

After all attempts, if $P_{\rm pos}$ is false, return
`nonpositive-predicted-decrease-budget`. If $P_{\rm pos}$ is true but
$P_{\rm dom}$ is false, return `domain-exit`: no SOC or ordinary trial could
be evaluated in $U$. Otherwise return `line-search-budget-exhausted`. These
finite tests do not guarantee acceptance or convergence.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The smooth program, an exact QP subproblem result, merit
parameters in the stated ranges, and finite positive caps.

[F1] [[alg-sqp-exhaustive-active-set-qp-solve]] returns a finite exact
subproblem status and, on success, a feasible linearized step, full QP
multiplier vectors, and the independent row sets $E$ and $J$.

[F2] [[def-sqp-l1-exact-penalty-merit]] defines $D_\rho$, $\psi_\rho$,
and the Armijo inequality used by the tests.

[F3] [[alg-sqp-second-order-correction]] returns a corrected point or a
failure status for the selected active constraints.

[A1] $\rho_0>0$, $\gamma>1$, $0<\beta,\sigma<1$, and the integer caps
$R,J_{\max}$ are positive and finite.

## Proof

1.1 On a successful QP return, the step is fixed before the penalty loop. For each index $r$ the positive scalar $\rho_r$ is defined, and [F2] defines a finite $D_r$ at $x$. Thus the branch $D_r\le0$ or $D_r>0$ is well-defined. [given, A1, F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 On each positive-prediction attempt, the routine performs at most one correction call and at most $J_{\max}$ ordinary trial tests; each in-domain test either returns its accepted record or advances a finite loop. There are at most $R$ attempts, so the total number of correction calls and ordinary tests is finite. The flags distinguish no positive prediction, positive prediction with no in-domain trial, and in-domain trials that all fail the Armijo test, giving respectively the nonpositive-prediction, domain-exit, and line-search-budget-exhausted statuses. No step asserts a passing trial or an asymptotic convergence property. [given, A1, F2, F3, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

For the SQP subproblem of [[def-sqp-linearized-quadratic-subproblem]] with
$B$ symmetric positive definite, the exact algorithm of
[[alg-sqp-exhaustive-active-set-qp-solve]] terminates after finitely many
subset tests. It returns `QP-infeasible` exactly when the subproblem's
polyhedron is empty; otherwise it returns the unique global minimizer, full
equality and inequality multiplier vectors, and the retained equality basis
$E$ and inequality support $J$ of its KKT certificate.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The exact-arithmetic algorithm and a subproblem with positive-
definite $B$.

[A1] The equality rows retained by the algorithm are independent and their
right-hand sides define the same consistent equality set as the original rows.

[F1] [[lem-sqp-convex-quadratic-subproblem-has-unique-kkt-certificate]]:
feasibility gives a unique minimizer with a KKT certificate supported on a
set of active rows independent together with the equality rows.

[F2] [[lem-sqp-kkt-matrix-nonsingularity-under-reduced-curvature]]: if the
active/equality rows are independent and $B$ is positive definite on their
null space, the KKT matrix is nonsingular.

[F3] [[alg-sqp-exhaustive-active-set-qp-solve]] tests every inequality subset
in a finite order and accepts only feasible candidates with nonnegative
selected inequality multipliers; it returns their multipliers expanded to the
original equality and inequality indices, together with $E$ and $J$.

## Proof

1.1 The equality reduction is finite: there are finitely many row subsets to check, and exact rank and consistency tests decide each one. Under [A1] it preserves the equality feasible set; if it reports inconsistency, that set is empty and the full QP is infeasible. [A1, F3, algebra]

1.2 For any enumerated subset whose rows are independent, the KKT matrix is nonsingular by [F2], because $B$ is positive definite on every subspace. Thus its equality-constrained candidate is uniquely defined. If that candidate passes the inequality feasibility and multiplier-sign filters, its zero-extended multipliers give a feasible KKT tuple for the original QP, so [F1] identifies it with the unique global minimizer. [F1, F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 If the QP is feasible, [F1] supplies an active KKT support whose rows are independent together with the reduced equality rows. [F3] therefore tests that support. The solve in step 1.2 returns its KKT point, and its feasibility and nonnegative multipliers make it pass both filters. Hence the algorithm cannot report `QP-infeasible` on a feasible subproblem. [A1, F1, F2, F3]

3.1 There are exactly $2^m$ inequality subsets. Every subset requires only finitely many exact rank, solve, and feasibility operations, so [F3] terminates. If no candidate was found, step 2.1 shows the QP is infeasible; if a candidate was found, step 1.2 shows it is the unique minimizer with the returned full KKT multipliers and support data. [F1, F3, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1] ∎

kind: theorem
title: "A feasible working-set QP solve terminates under nondegenerate steps"
status: draft
origin: pipeline

dependency_level: 4

      url: https://www.ime.unicamp.br/~pulino/MT404/TextosOnline/NocedalJ.pdf
      locator: "Chapter 16 §16.4, Theorems 16.4–16.5 and finite termination of Algorithm 16.1, printed pp. 457–465 / PDF pp. 477–484."
---

## Statement

Consider a feasible SQP quadratic subproblem with $B\succ0$, $m$ inequality
rows, and $r$ independent equality rows. Run
[[alg-sqp-feasible-working-set-qp-solve]] with an independent initial working
set and cap $N\ge(n+2)2^m$. Assume exact subproblem solves, every nonzero
working-set direction has a strictly positive maximal feasible step, and a
blocker is selected by the algorithm's least-index tie rule. Then the
algorithm returns the unique global minimizer and a KKT certificate in at
most $N$ iterations. If a zero blocking step, dependent blocker, failed solve,
or smaller user cap occurs, the algorithm returns its stated inconclusive
status and no optimality claim follows.

The positive-step hypothesis is the nondegeneracy condition that prevents
zero-length working-set cycling. The proof also shows that a working set
already minimized with negative multipliers cannot recur after progress.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The feasible QP, exact arithmetic, the working-set algorithm, and
the hypotheses in the Statement.

[A1] $B$ is symmetric positive definite; all active/equality rows in the
current working set are independent; every nonzero direction has $\alpha>0$.

[F1] [[alg-sqp-feasible-working-set-qp-solve]] solves the strictly convex
quadratic on the current working-set face, takes the largest feasible step,
adds a least-index blocker, and deletes a least-index negative-multiplier row.

[F2] [[lem-sqp-kkt-matrix-nonsingularity-under-reduced-curvature]] makes each
working-set KKT system nonsingular when its rows are independent.

[F3] [[lem-sqp-convex-quadratic-subproblem-has-unique-kkt-certificate]]: a
feasible strictly convex QP has a unique minimizer, and any feasible KKT tuple
is a global certificate.

## Proof

1.1 Let $z$ be a feasible iterate, $W$ its working set, and $u\ne0$ the exact direction minimizer. Its KKT equation is $Bu+(Bz+c)+A^T\nu+\sum_{i\in W}\mu_iG_i^T=0$, with $Au=0$ and $G_iu=0$ for $i\in W$. Multiplying by $u^T$ gives $(Bz+c)^Tu=-u^TBu$. Hence for every accepted $0<\alpha\le1$, $$q(z+\alpha u)-q(z)=-\alpha(1-\alpha/2)u^TBu<0.$$ If $\alpha<1$, a blocking row cannot lie in the span of the current rows, since it has $G_iu>0$ while every row in that span annihilates $u$; adding it preserves independence. [A1, F1, F2, algebra]

1.2 Suppose instead $u=0$ and the multiplier of a working inequality $j$ is negative. After deleting $j$, let $v$ be the next exact direction. The new direction stationarity, dotted with $v$, gives $(Bz+c)^Tv=-v^TBv$. The old face stationarity, also dotted with $v$, gives $(Bz+c)^Tv+\mu_jG_jv=0$, because all retained working rows annihilate $v$. Therefore $\mu_jG_jv=v^TBv>0$, so $v\ne0$ and $G_jv<0$. The dropped inequality is feasible to first order, and by the positive-step hypothesis the next iterate moves strictly along this descent direction. [A1, F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 For a fixed working set $W$, positive definiteness makes the face objective have at most one minimizer. Once the algorithm reaches that face minimizer, either all working inequality multipliers are nonnegative and it terminates, or step 1.2 gives a strict objective decrease after a negative multiplier is dropped. Every later iterate is then below the minimum value on that face, so the same working set cannot be face-minimized again. There are at most $2^m$ working sets. [A1, step 1.1, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 Between successive face minimizers, each nonterminal partial step adds an independent blocker, so there can be at most $n-r$ such additions before the feasible direction space is zero. A full step with no blocker reaches a face minimizer immediately. Thus each of the at most $2^m$ face-minimization episodes uses at most $n-r+2\le n+2$ iterations. The cap $N\ge(n+2)2^m$ cannot be reached before a terminal KKT point. [step 2.1, F1, induction, algebra]

4.1 At termination, feasibility is maintained and every working inequality multiplier is nonnegative; assign zero multipliers to inequalities outside the working set. This is a KKT tuple, so [F3] makes it the global minimizer, and strict convexity in [A1] makes that minimizer unique. If a degeneracy or cap status occurs instead, the algorithm reports no KKT certificate, as stated. [A1, F1, F3, step 3.1] ∎

## Statement

Let $c_A:U\to\mathbb R^r$ with $r\ge1$ be $C^2$ on a convex ball about $x$, and assume
$\|D^2c_A(z)[u,v]\|_2\le M\|u\|_2\|v\|_2$ throughout that ball. Let
$A=Dc_A(x)$ have smallest singular value at least $s_0>0$, and let $p$ be
small enough that $x+p$ and the correction segment stay in the ball. If
$c_A(x)+Ap=0$ and $w$ is the correction of
[[alg-sqp-second-order-correction]], then
$$\|w\|_2\le\frac{M}{2s_0}\|p\|_2^2, \qquad \|c_A(x+p+w)\|_2=O(\|p\|_2^3)\quad(p\to0).$$
The correction is the unique minimum-norm vector satisfying
$Aw=-c_A(x+p)$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The $C^2$ active constraint map, bounded second derivative,
uniform row rank, and a step satisfying the linearized active equations.

[F1] [[alg-sqp-second-order-correction]] sets
$w=-A^T(AA^T)^{-1}c_A(x+p)$ and proves it is the minimum-norm solution of
$Aw=-c_A(x+p)$.

[F2] [[cor-second-order-taylor-expansion-with-the-hessian]] gives the
second-order Taylor expansion with a remainder $o(\|p\|_2^2)$ for $C^2$
maps, componentwise.

[A1] The smallest singular value of $A$ is at least $s_0>0$, the second
derivative bound is $M$, and the trial and correction segments lie in the
convex ball.

## Proof

1.1 Taylor's formula along $x+tp$ and the bound on $D^2c_A$ give $$c_A(x+p)=c_A(x)+Ap+R_p=R_p,\qquad \|R_p\|_2\le\frac M2\|p\|_2^2.$$ Since $\|A^T(AA^T)^{-1}\|_2=1/s_{\min}(A)\le1/s_0$, [F1] yields $\|w\|_2\le M\|p\|_2^2/(2s_0)$ and $c_A(x+p)+Aw=0$. [given, F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 Put $y=x+p$. Taylor expansion at $y$ gives $$c_A(y+w)=c_A(y)+Dc_A(y)w+R_w =\bigl(Dc_A(y)-A\bigr)w+R_w,$$ where $\|Dc_A(y)-A\|_2\le M\|p\|_2$ and $\|R_w\|_2\le M\|w\|_2^2/2$. Therefore $$\|c_A(y+w)\|_2\le M\|p\|_2\|w\|_2+\tfrac M2\|w\|_2^2 \le \frac{M^2}{2s_0}\|p\|_2^3+\frac{M^3}{8s_0^2}\|p\|_2^4,$$ which is $O(\|p\|_2^3)$ for small $p$. The minimum-norm assertion is [F1]. [given, F1, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Let $x_*$ be a KKT point of a $C^2$ nonlinear program, with multiplier
$\mu_*=(\nu_*,\lambda_{*,I})$ and active set $I=I(x_*)$. Assume LICQ,
strict complementarity $\lambda_{*,i}>0$ for every $i\in I$, and the
second-order sufficient condition
$$d^T\nabla^2_{xx}L(x_*,\mu_*)d>0 \quad\text{for every nonzero critical direction }d.$$
Assume also that the active KKT map $F_A$ has a locally Lipschitz
Jacobian: on some ball, $\|DF_A(z)-DF_A(z\prime)\|_2\le L\|z-z\prime\|_2$.
Once the correct active set is used, exact arithmetic full steps of
[[alg-sqp-exact-hessian-newton-step]], started sufficiently close to
$(x_*,\mu_*)$, are well-defined and converge quadratically to that pair.
This is the local full-step Newton result; it does not assert acceptance by
an L1 merit line search.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The smooth program, a KKT pair, LICQ, strict complementarity,
the stated second-order sufficient condition, a locally identified active
set, and the locally Lipschitz Jacobian hypothesis.

[F1] [[def-inequality-constrained-program-and-kkt-geometry]] defines the
KKT system, LICQ, active set, and critical cone in the $g\le0$ convention.

[F2] [[lem-sqp-kkt-matrix-nonsingularity-under-reduced-curvature]]: if
active rows are independent and the Lagrangian Hessian is positive on their
null space, the active KKT Jacobian is nonsingular.

[F3] [[alg-sqp-exact-hessian-newton-step]] solves the exact Newton equation
for the active KKT map and takes the full step.

[F4] [[thm-inexact-newton-local-forcing-rates]] gives local quadratic
convergence for a $C^1$ root map with Lipschitz Jacobian and invertible root
Jacobian when the Newton residual is zero.

[A1] The program is $C^2$, LICQ holds, all active inequality multipliers
are strictly positive, the Lagrangian Hessian is positive on every
nonzero critical direction, and the active KKT map has a locally
Lipschitz Jacobian near the root.

## Proof

1.1 Let $A$ stack equality rows and active inequality rows at $x_*$. For $d\in\ker A$, $d$ is linearly feasible and has zero derivative on every active inequality. Conversely, if $d$ is in the critical cone, stationarity gives $\nabla f(x_*)^Td=-\sum_{i\in I}\lambda_{*,i}Dg_i(x_*)d$; each $Dg_i(x_*)d\le0$, so equality to zero and strict positivity of every $\lambda_{*,i}$ force each such derivative to vanish. Thus the critical cone is exactly $\ker A$. The stated second-order condition gives positive curvature on $\ker A$, and LICQ gives independent rows. [given, F1, algebra]

2.1 Define $F(x,\mu)=(\nabla_xL(x,\mu),c_A(x))$. Its derivative at the root is the active KKT block matrix, nonsingular by [F2] and step 1.1. By [A1], this derivative is locally Lipschitz on a small ball. The exact step of [F3] satisfies $DF(x_k,\mu_k)s_k+F(x_k,\mu_k)=0$. Apply [F4] to the combined primal-dual variable: for a sufficiently close starting pair, all full steps are defined, remain local, and converge quadratically. [given, A1, F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

title: "Reduced-BFGS SQP is locally superlinear under reduced Dennis-More and inverse bounds"
status: draft

      locator: "Chapter 18 §18.10, Theorems 18.5–18.8, printed pp. 563–564 / PDF pp. 581–582; projected Dennis–Moré and reduced-Hessian rates."
---

## Statement

Let $F_A$ be the active KKT map defined in
[[alg-sqp-exact-hessian-newton-step]]. Let the program be $C^2$, with a
correct locally identified active set,
LICQ, strict complementarity, and the second-order sufficient condition.
Assume the active KKT map $F_A$ has a locally Lipschitz Jacobian near the
solution. At each nonterminal iterate let $P_k$ project onto
$\ker A_k$, where $A_k=Dc_A(x_k)$ is the Jacobian of the identified
active constraints. Set $z_k=(x_k,\mu_k)$,
$F_k=F_A(z_k)$, $J_k=DF_A(z_k)$, and
$s_k=(p_k,\delta\mu_k)$ for the computed reduced-BFGS step. Let $H_k$ be
the exact Lagrangian Hessian and $B_k$ the symmetric positive-definite
model. Suppose the reduced-BFGS KKT matrices
$\widetilde J_k$ are nonsingular with
$\sup_k\|\widetilde J_k^{-1}\|_2<\infty$, and the reduced Dennis–Moré
condition holds along the computed primal steps $p_k$:
$$\frac{\|P_k(B_k-H_k)P_kp_k\|_2}{\|p_k\|_2}\longrightarrow0 \quad\text{whenever }p_k\ne0.$$
Also assume the exact Newton residual ratios satisfy
$\|J_ks_k+F_k\|_2\le\bar\eta\|F_k\|_2$ for every nonterminal $k$, for
some fixed $\bar\eta<1$.
Then full steps of [[alg-sqp-reduced-bfgs-kkt-step]] started sufficiently
near the KKT pair converge superlinearly, unless an exact root is reached
first. No globalization or global BFGS convergence claim is made.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The active KKT regularity hypotheses, symmetric positive
definite models, uniform inverse bound, and the reduced Dennis–Moré limit.

[F1] [[def-inequality-constrained-program-and-kkt-geometry]] defines the
active KKT equations and the $g\le0$ multiplier convention.

[F2] [[lem-sqp-kkt-matrix-nonsingularity-under-reduced-curvature]] makes
the exact KKT Jacobian nonsingular under LICQ and positive reduced curvature.

[F3] [[alg-sqp-reduced-bfgs-kkt-step]] replaces only the tangent Hessian
block by $H_k+P_k(B_k-H_k)P_k$ and solves the resulting KKT system.

[F4] [[thm-inexact-newton-local-forcing-rates]] gives local superlinear
convergence when the Newton residual is $o(\|F_k\|_2)$ and the exact root
Jacobian is invertible with locally Lipschitz derivative.

[A1] The program is $C^2$, LICQ and strict complementarity hold at the
solution, the reduced Hessian is positive on the tangent space, the active
KKT map has a locally Lipschitz Jacobian, the approximate KKT inverse norms
are uniformly bounded, the stated reduced Dennis–Moré ratios tend to zero,
and all exact Newton residual ratios are bounded by $\bar\eta<1$.

## Proof

1.1 Set $z_k=(x_k,\mu_k)$ and $F_k=F(z_k)$ for the active KKT map. The exact Jacobian $J_k=DF(z_k)$ has upper-left block $H_k$. By [F3], the computed step $s_k=(p_k,\delta\mu_k)$ solves $\widetilde J_ks_k=-F_k$, where $\widetilde J_k$ differs from $J_k$ only by replacing that block with $H_k+P_k(B_k-H_k)P_k$. Hence the exact Newton residual is $$r_k:=J_ks_k+F_k=\binom{-P_k(B_k-H_k)P_kp_k}{0}.$$ [given, F1, F3, algebra]

2.1 The inverse bound gives $\|s_k\|_2\le C\|F_k\|_2$ and therefore $\|p_k\|_2\le C\|F_k\|_2$. The Dennis–Moré condition supplies numbers $\delta_k\to0$ with $\|r_k\|_2\le\delta_k\|p_k\|_2$ whenever $p_k\ne0$; therefore $\|r_k\|_2\le C\delta_k\|F_k\|_2$. At a zero primal step the displayed residual is zero, so the same conclusion holds. [given, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 LICQ and the second-order condition make $J_*$ nonsingular by [F2], as in the exact-Hessian result. The Jacobian is locally Lipschitz by [A1]. Thus the steps satisfy the inexact-Newton equation with forcing factor $\eta_k:=\|r_k\|_2/\|F_k\|_2$ when $F_k\ne0$, and $\eta_k:=0$ when $F_k=0$. Assumption [A1] gives $\eta_k\le\bar\eta<1$, while step 2.1 gives $\eta_k\le C\delta_k\to0$. [A1, F2, F4, step 2.1]

4.1 Apply [F4] to the combined primal-dual variable. Starting sufficiently near the root, the full steps remain local and converge superlinearly. If an exact root is reached, no further convergence assertion is needed; if the algorithm reports a failed solve, its nonsingularity hypotheses have failed and this theorem does not apply. [F3, F4, step 3.1] ∎

id: thm-sqp-augmented-lagrangian-local-convergence
kind: theorem
title: "Augmented-Lagrangian multipliers converge locally with summable inner residuals"
status: draft
origin: pipeline
pipeline_run: numerical-optimization-dynamics-2026-10-16
dependency_level: 3
deps:
  - def-sqp-augmented-lagrangian-equality-and-inequality

      locator: "Chapter 2 §§2.2.2 and 2.2.4, printed pp. 107–112 and 115–121; local augmented-Lagrangian minima, multiplier convergence, and the need to remain on the local minimizer branch."
    - title: "Jorge Nocedal and Stephen J. Wright, Numerical Optimization, 2nd ed."
      url: https://www.ime.unicamp.br/~pulino/MT404/TextosOnline/NocedalJ.pdf
      locator: "Chapter 17 §17.4, printed pp. 511–521 / PDF pp. 529–539."
---

## Statement

Let $x_*$ be a KKT point of a $C^2$ program with active inequality set
$I=I(x_*)$, multiplier $\mu_*=(\nu_*,\lambda_{*,I})$, and active
constraint vector $c=(h,g_I)$. Assume LICQ, strict complementarity
$\lambda_{*,i}>0$ for $i\in I$, and the second-order sufficient condition
$d^TH_*d>0$ for every nonzero $d\in\ker A_*$, where
$A_*=Dc(x_*)$ and $H_*=\nabla^2_{xx}L(x_*,\mu_*)$.

For all sufficiently large fixed $\rho$, the PHR augmented-Lagrangian
multiplier update has a local contraction when each inner minimization is
solved exactly. When $r>0$, the same local multiplier convergence holds for inner
points $\widehat x_k$ with stationarity residuals
$\epsilon_k=\|\nabla_x\mathcal L_\rho(\widehat x_k,\nu_k,\lambda_k)\|_2$
whose sum is sufficiently small, provided each point stays in the local
strongly convex branch. More precisely, there are local radii $\delta_\mu$
and $d_x>0$, a strong-convexity constant $\alpha>0$, and a contraction
factor $q<1$ such that convergence holds whenever
$$\|\mu_0-\mu_*\|_2\le\delta_\mu/2,\qquad \sum_{k=0}^\infty\epsilon_k\le \min\left\{\alpha d_x,\frac{(1-q)\delta_\mu}{2C}\right\},$$
where $C=\rho L_c/\alpha$ and $L_c$ is a Lipschitz constant for $c$ on
the local primal neighborhood. Inactive multipliers are initialized at
zero. If $c$ has zero components, the multiplier update is absent and the
bound involving $C$ is omitted; sufficiently local inner points with
summable residuals converge to $x_*$ by strong convexity.

This is a limit theorem for an infinite sequence of successful inner
returns. The contraction estimates apply to any successful prefix of the
finite-budget procedure; the limit conclusion applies only to an infinite
continuation whose calls continue to return within their finite inner caps.
For that procedure, the residual sequence in this theorem is the reported
$\widehat\epsilon_k$; its input tolerances must be chosen so these reports
satisfy the displayed summability bound.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The $C^2$ program, KKT pair, LICQ, strict complementarity,
positive curvature on $\ker A_*$, fixed $\rho$, and summable inner residuals.

[F1] [[def-inequality-constrained-program-and-kkt-geometry]] defines
LICQ, KKT stationarity, and the $g\le0$, $\lambda\ge0$ convention.

[F2] [[def-sqp-augmented-lagrangian-equality-and-inequality]] defines the
PHR Lagrangian and projected multiplier update.

[F3] [[thm-euclidean-implicit-function-theorem]] gives a local $C^1$
solution branch for a $C^1$ equation with invertible derivative and the
derivative formula for that branch.

[F4] [[alg-sqp-augmented-lagrangian-multiplier-method]] uses the displayed
inner stationarity residual and projected multiplier update, with finite
inner and outer caps and explicit exhaustion/failure returns.

[A1] LICQ holds; every active inequality multiplier is strictly positive;
the Lagrangian Hessian is positive definite on $\ker A_*$; inactive
multipliers start at zero; and inner points stay in a neighborhood where
the PHR branches used below remain fixed.

[A2] Every inner call in the sequence under consideration returns
successfully within its finite cap with the stated residual; an
inner-budget-exhausted or inner-failure status ends the finite procedure and
is not a convergence step.

## Proof

1.1 Write $A=A_*$, $H=H_*$ and $r=\dim c$. Strict complementarity and continuity give a neighborhood in which every active inequality satisfies $\lambda_i+\rho g_i(x)>0$ and every inactive inequality, whose multiplier is initialized at zero, satisfies $\lambda_j+\rho g_j(x)<0$. On this branch, [F2] reduces the $x$-dependent augmented Lagrangian to $$\Phi_\rho(x,\mu)=f(x)+\mu^Tc(x)+\frac\rho2\|c(x)\|_2^2,$$ where $\mu=(\nu,\lambda_I)$. Its gradient vanishes at $(x_*,\mu_*)$. [given, F1, F2, algebra, algebra]

1.2 The $x$-Hessian at the base point is $W_\rho=H+\rho A^TA$. If $r=0$, the assumed condition says $H\succ0$. For $r>0$, choose orthonormal matrices $Z,Y$ spanning $\ker A$ and its orthogonal complement, respectively; then $C_0=AY$ is invertible. In this basis the tangent block is $H_T=Z^THZ\succ0$ when its dimension is positive, the cross blocks are those of $H$, and the normal block is $Y^THY+\rho C_0^TC_0$. Its Schur complement over the tangent block is $D+\rho C_0^TC_0$, where $D=Y^THY-Y^THZ H_T^{-1}Z^THY$; if the tangent block is empty, take $D=Y^THY$. Since $C_0^TC_0\succ0$, this Schur complement is positive definite for sufficiently large $\rho$. Hence $W_\rho\succ0$. [given, algebra, choose]

2.1 If $r>0$, apply [F3] to $G(x,\mu)=\nabla_x\Phi_\rho(x,\mu)=0$. Its $x$ derivative is $W_\rho$, which is invertible by step 1.2, and its $\mu$ derivative is $A^T$. Therefore there is a local $C^1$ branch $x(\mu)$ with $x(\mu_*)=x_*$ and $$Dx(\mu_*)=-W_\rho^{-1}A^T.$$ If $r=0$, the empty-multiplier branch consists of the local minimizer $x_*$. By continuity of the Hessian, after shrinking to a convex neighborhood $\Phi_\rho(\cdot,\mu)$ is uniformly strongly convex there; its stationary branch point is its unique local minimizer. [F3, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 For $r>0$, the exact multiplier map is $T(\mu)=\mu+\rho c(x(\mu))$, so $$DT(\mu_*)=I-\rho A W_\rho^{-1}A^T.$$ In the orthonormal coordinates of step 1.2, block elimination gives $A W_\rho^{-1}A^T=C_0(D+\rho C_0^TC_0)^{-1}C_0^T$ $=(\rho I+E)^{-1}$, where $E=C_0^{-T}DC_0^{-1}$ is symmetric. Thus $DT(\mu_*)=E(\rho I+E)^{-1}$. Its eigenvalues are $e_i/(\rho+e_i)$, which have absolute value less than $1$ for all sufficiently large $\rho$. Continuity of $DT$ then gives a closed multiplier ball on which $T$ is a contraction with some factor $q<1$. For $r=0$ the multiplier update is absent. [step 1.2, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Let $\widehat x_k$ be an inner point in the selected branch with residual at most $\epsilon_k$, and let $x(\mu_k)$ be the exact branch minimizer. Strong convexity with constant $\alpha$ gives $$\alpha\|\widehat x_k-x(\mu_k)\|_2^2\le \langle\nabla\Phi_\rho(\widehat x_k,\mu_k)- \nabla\Phi_\rho(x(\mu_k),\mu_k),\widehat x_k-x(\mu_k)\rangle \le\epsilon_k\|\widehat x_k-x(\mu_k)\|_2.$$ After cancellation (with the zero-distance case immediate), $\|\widehat x_k-x(\mu_k)\|_2\le\epsilon_k/\alpha$. The multiplier update is on the same PHR branch, so its difference from $T(\mu_k)$ has norm at most $\rho L_c\epsilon_k/\alpha=C\epsilon_k$. Hence $$\|\mu_{k+1}-\mu_*\|_2\le q\|\mu_k-\mu_*\|_2+C\epsilon_k.$$ The stated sum bound keeps this recurrence inside the multiplier ball and keeps every inner point within the primal branch tube. [A1, A2, F2, F4, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 Iterating the inequality gives $$\|\mu_k-\mu_*\|_2\le q^k\|\mu_0-\mu_*\|_2+ C\sum_{j=0}^{k-1}q^{k-1-j}\epsilon_j.$$ The first term tends to zero. For the sum, any fixed finite prefix tends to zero as $k\to\infty$, while the remaining tail is bounded by $C\sum_{j\ge J}\epsilon_j$, which tends to zero as $J\to\infty$. Therefore $\mu_k\to\mu_*$. Also $\epsilon_k\to0$ because it is summable, so step 4.1 gives $\widehat x_k-x(\mu_k)\to0$ and continuity gives $\widehat x_k\to x_*$. When $r=0$, step 1.2 gives a strongly convex local objective and the same residual estimate directly yields $\widehat x_k\to x_*$. [given, A1, A2, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 The hypotheses and local restrictions used above are exactly the regularity, branch, residual, and successful-inner-call conditions in the Statement and [A2]. This proves the limit claim for the successful update sequence; a finite dispatch may return a cap or failure status first and no global convergence is asserted. [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 4.1, step 5.1] ∎

## Definition

Let $K=\begin{bmatrix}H&A^T\\A&0\end{bmatrix}\in\mathbb R^{N\times N}$
be an active KKT matrix, where $A$ has full row rank and $H$ is positive
definite on $\ker A$, and let $b\in\mathbb R^N$. By
[[lem-sqp-kkt-matrix-nonsingularity-under-reduced-curvature]], $K$ is
nonsingular. Also supply a terminating exact-storage routine which, for each requested real entry, either returns that same value with an exact representability certificate in the selected floating-point set or returns `unavailable`. Before QR, invoke this routine on every entry of the intended $K$ and $b$, in increasing row and column order for $K$ and increasing index for $b$. If any call is unavailable or its equality/representability certificate is not verified, return `numerical-failure` without a solve certificate. Otherwise use these unchanged stored values, still denoted $K,b$, for both the solve and residual evaluation. No rounded conversion is performed: every successful residual certificate below concerns the original intended data. Assume $Nu<1$, $\gamma_{N+3}<1/8$, and the successful-operation
hypotheses of
[[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]],
run scaled Householder QR and rounded back substitution as in
[[thm-computed-full-rank-least-squares-backward-stability]]. If factorization
or substitution fails, return `numerical-failure`.

For a returned stored vector $\widehat z$, compute in the specified order
$\widehat v=\operatorname{fl}(K\widehat z)$ and
$\widehat r=\operatorname{fl}(\widehat v-b)$. Use
[[lem-rounded-linear-and-normal-residual-certificates]] with $A=K$,
$x=\widehat z$, and $y=b$ to compute
$$g_N=\frac{1+6u}{1-(N-1)u}-1,\qquad W=g_N\|K\|_F\|\widehat z\|_2+u(\|\widehat v\|_2+\|b\|_2),$$
where the product and subtraction use successful sequential dot products
and $(N-1)u<1$. Let $\kappa_N$ be the local coefficient specified by
[[lem-scaled-householder-step-meets-local-backward-error-premise]], and set
$$\beta_Q=(1+\kappa_N)^N-1,\qquad \beta_b=\beta_Q,\qquad \beta_K=\beta_Q+\gamma_{N+3}(1+\beta_Q),$$
where $\gamma_j=ju/(1-ju)$ is defined by the operationwise model. The QR
theorem supplies an exactly orthonormal $\widehat Q$, a triangular
$\widehat R$, and perturbations satisfying
$$K+\Delta_Q=\widehat Q\widehat R,\quad (\widehat R+\Delta_R)\widehat z=\widehat Q^T(b+\delta b),$$
with $\|\Delta_Q\|_F\le\beta_Q\|K\|_F$,
$\|\Delta_R\|_F\le\gamma_{N+3}\|\widehat R\|_F$, and
$\|\delta b\|_2\le\beta_b\|b\|_2$. Define
$\Delta_K=\Delta_Q+\widehat Q\Delta_R$. Return
$$\eta=\min\left\{\|\widehat r\|_2+W, \beta_K\|K\|_F\|\widehat z\|_2+\beta_b\|b\|_2\right\}$$
using exact norms or certified upward bounds. If residual evaluation or a
certified bound fails, return `numerical-failure`. A successful return
certifies a residual upper bound, not a small residual or an accurate exact
solution by itself.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A nonsingular square KKT matrix, right-hand side, floating-point
model hypotheses, and successful QR and triangular solves.

[F1] [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]]
states the operationwise rounding hypotheses and successful-operation
convention.

[F2] [[thm-computed-full-rank-least-squares-backward-stability]] supplies
$K+\Delta_Q=\widehat Q\widehat R$ with exactly orthonormal $\widehat Q$,
the rounded triangular solve
$(\widehat R+\Delta_R)\widehat z=\widehat Q^T(b+\delta b)$, and the stated
perturbation bounds.

[F3] [[lem-rounded-linear-and-normal-residual-certificates]]: for the
specified rounded product and subtraction,
$\|\widehat r-(K\widehat z-b)\|_2\le W$.

[F4] [[lem-sqp-kkt-matrix-nonsingularity-under-reduced-curvature]] makes
the input KKT matrix nonsingular under the stated rank and curvature
hypotheses.

[F5] [[lem-scaled-householder-step-meets-local-backward-error-premise]]
defines the local coefficient $\kappa_N$ used in the QR backward bound.

[A1] The terminating exact-storage admission has succeeded and its stored $K,b$ equal the intended inputs entrywise. Also $N\ge1$, $Nu<1$, $\gamma_{N+3}<1/8$, $(N-1)u<1$, all factorization
and residual operations succeed under the operationwise model, and any norm
upper bounds used in $\eta$ are certified without overflow.

## Proof

1.1 The admission in [A1] supplies stored $K,b$ equal to the intended data; the factorization and transformed right-hand side are therefore admissible stored operands. By [F4], $K$ is nonsingular and, being square, has full column rank, so the perturbation equations of [F2] apply under [A1]. Their additional perturbed-least-squares uniqueness condition is not needed for this residual calculation. Multiplying the triangular equation by $\widehat Q$ and using $\widehat Q\widehat Q^T=I$ gives $\widehat Q(\widehat R+\Delta_R)\widehat z=b+\delta b$. Substituting $\widehat Q\widehat R=K+\Delta_Q$ yields $(K+\Delta_K)\widehat z=b+\delta b$ for $\Delta_K=\Delta_Q+\widehat Q\Delta_R$. Orthogonality gives $\|\widehat Q\Delta_R\|_F=\|\Delta_R\|_F$, and $\|\widehat R\|_F=\|K+\Delta_Q\|_F\le(1+\beta_Q)\|K\|_F$. Hence $$\|\Delta_K\|_F\le \bigl(\beta_Q+\gamma_{N+3}(1+\beta_Q)\bigr)\|K\|_F =\beta_K\|K\|_F.$$ Rearrangement now gives $$\|K\widehat z-b\|_2\le \|\delta b\|_2+\|\Delta_K\|_F\|\widehat z\|_2 \le\beta_b\|b\|_2+\beta_K\|K\|_F\|\widehat z\|_2.$$ [given, A1, F1, F2, F4, F5, algebra]

2.1 By [F3] and the triangle inequality, $$\|K\widehat z-b\|_2\le\|\widehat r\|_2+W.$$ Both entries in the returned minimum are upper bounds, so their minimum is also an upper bound. Failure of any required operation exits without a certificate. [given, A1, F1, F3, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

For finite caps $R,J_{\max}\ge1$ and finite-valued merit evaluations, the
procedure of [[alg-sqp-merit-globalization-with-finite-budgets]] terminates with
exactly one of its specified accepted, QP, nonpositive-prediction,
domain-exit, or line-search-budget statuses. Each accepted record contains
the trial point and QP multiplier vectors; an ordinary accepted record also
contains its fraction. In particular, the theorem asserts no unconditional
accepted step.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The globalization algorithm, finite positive caps, and
well-defined finite arithmetic evaluations at every tested in-domain point.

[F1] [[alg-sqp-merit-globalization-with-finite-budgets]] performs at most
$R$ penalty attempts and at most $J_{\max}$ ordinary trial tests per
attempt, plus at most one optional in-domain SOC test per attempt, and
records whether any positive prediction and any in-domain trial test
occurred.

[A1] The caps $R,J_{\max}$ are positive finite integers and every in-domain
merit evaluation terminates with a finite value.

## Proof

1.1 The exact QP routine in [F1] tests at most $2^m$ subsets, so it returns a QP status after finitely many tests. A returned infeasible or failure status terminates immediately. Otherwise each penalty attempt computes one finite prediction and either advances or executes a finite list of tests. [A1, F1, algebra]

2.1 There are at most $R(1+J_{\max})$ globalization tests. A passing test returns an accepted record. If none passes, the stored flags select exactly one of the nonpositive-prediction, domain-exit, or line-search-budget-exhausted statuses according to whether any positive prediction and any in-domain test occurred. Thus the routine terminates with a defined status, without implying that any test must pass. [A1, F1, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Suppose [[alg-sqp-finite-precision-kkt-qr-solve-and-residual-check]]
successfully returns $\widehat z$ and a certified $\eta$ for a nonsingular
square matrix $K$ and vector $b$. Then
$$\|K\widehat z-b\|_2\le\eta.$$
If $z_*=K^{-1}b$, then also
$$\|\widehat z-z_*\|_2\le\|K^{-1}\|_2\eta.$$
The certificate may be large; the theorem makes no accuracy claim without
an additional bound on $\|K^{-1}\|_2$ and a small certified $\eta$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The operationwise arithmetic hypotheses, successful reduced QR
and residual computation, and the returned certificate $\eta$.

[F1] [[alg-sqp-finite-precision-kkt-qr-solve-and-residual-check]] returns
the minimum of the rounded-residual and QR backward-error bounds.

[F2] [[lem-rounded-linear-and-normal-residual-certificates]] bounds the
difference between the exact residual and the computed rounded residual.

[F3] [[thm-computed-full-rank-least-squares-backward-stability]] supplies
the QR backward representation and its perturbation bounds.

[F4] [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]]
specifies the arithmetic assumptions required by [F2] and [F3].

[F5] [[lem-sqp-kkt-matrix-nonsingularity-under-reduced-curvature]] provides
nonsingularity for a full-row-rank active KKT matrix with positive reduced
curvature.

[A1] The KKT matrix has full-row-rank constraints and positive curvature on
their null space; all successful-operation hypotheses hold, and the stated
certificate is computed without overflow.

## Proof

1.1 By [F1], a successful return includes successful exact-storage admission, so its stored $K,b$ equal the intended data. By [F5], $K$ is nonsingular. Put $r=K\widehat z-b$ for those same intended data. By [F2], $\|r\|_2\le\|\widehat r\|_2+W$. By [F3], $r=\delta b-\Delta K\widehat z$, so $\|r\|_2\le\beta_b\|b\|_2+\beta_K\|K\|_F\|\widehat z\|_2$. These are precisely the two bounds in [F1]. [A1, F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, algebra]

2.1 Since [F1] returns their minimum, $\|K\widehat z-b\|_2\le\eta$. The exact solution satisfies $Kz_*=b$, hence $K(\widehat z-z_*)=r$; multiplying by $K^{-1}$ gives $\|\widehat z-z_*\|_2\le\|K^{-1}\|_2\|r\|_2\le\|K^{-1}\|_2\eta$. [F1, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Consider the design problem
$$\min_{x\in\mathbb R^2}\frac12(x_1^2+x_2^2) \quad\text{subject to }1-x_1-x_2\le0.$$
At $x_0=(0,0)$, use $B=I$ in the SQP quadratic subproblem. The exact
active-set solve returns $p=(1/2,1/2)$, and $x_0+p$ is the unique global
minimizer of the nonlinear problem, with active demand constraint and
multiplier $1/2$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The quadratic objective, linear demand constraint, and SQP
subproblem and exact active-set conventions.

[F1] [[def-sqp-linearized-quadratic-subproblem]] defines the SQP model as
the objective gradient plus a positive-definite quadratic term and affine
linearized constraints.

[F2] [[alg-sqp-exhaustive-active-set-qp-solve]] tests feasible active KKT
supports and returns an accepted exact candidate.

[F3] [[thm-sqp-exhaustive-active-set-qp-solve-correct-finite]] identifies
that candidate as the unique global QP minimizer.

[F4] [[thm-convex-kkt-sufficiency-and-normal-cone-certificate]]: a
feasible KKT tuple for a convex objective with affine constraints certifies
global optimality.

[A1] The SQP model matrix at $x_0$ is $I$, and all arithmetic is exact.

## Proof

1.1 At $x_0$, $\nabla f(x_0)=0$ and the linearized inequality is $1-p_1-p_2\le0$. The unconstrained minimizer $p=0$ is infeasible. On the active face $p_1+p_2=1$, stationarity for $q(p)=\tfrac12\|p\|_2^2$ is $p-\lambda(1,1)^T=0$; combining with the face equation gives $p_1=p_2=\lambda=1/2$. This point is feasible with nonnegative multiplier. [given, A1, F1, algebra]

2.1 The positive-definite QP has a unique minimizer; its feasible KKT tuple passes the active-set acceptance filters in [F2]. By [F3] the returned step is exactly $(1/2,1/2)$. [A1, F2, F3, step 1.1]

3.1 The nonlinear point $x_*=(1/2,1/2)$ is feasible and has $\nabla f(x_*)=(1/2,1/2)$, $\nabla g(x_*)=(-1,-1)$, and multiplier $\lambda_*=1/2$. Thus stationarity holds, the multiplier is nonnegative, and complementarity holds with $g(x_*)=0$. Since the objective is convex and the constraint affine, [F4] proves global optimality; strict convexity of the objective makes the minimizer unique. [F4, algebra, step 2.1] ∎

## Statement

Let $h(x)=x_1^2+x_2^2-1=0$ and
$f(x)=2(x_1^2+x_2^2-1)-x_1$. At a feasible point
$x=(\cos\theta,\sin\theta)=(c,s)$, use multiplier estimate $\nu=-3/2$
and SQP Hessian model $B=I$. For nonzero sufficiently small $\theta$, the
SQP step $p=(s^2,-sc)$ has predicted decrease $D_\rho=s^2>0$, but its full
step increases the L1 merit for every $\rho>0$. The minimum-norm SOC
correction makes the full corrected step pass the Armijo test with
$\sigma=1/4$ for every fixed $\rho>0$ and all sufficiently small nonzero
$\theta$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The equality-constrained SQP and L1 merit definitions, the SOC
formula, and $c=\cos\theta$, $s=\sin\theta$.

[F1] [[def-sqp-linearized-quadratic-subproblem]] imposes
$h(x)+Dh(x)p=0$ in the subproblem.

[F2] [[def-sqp-l1-exact-penalty-merit]] defines the merit and predicted
decrease $D_\rho$.

[F3] [[alg-sqp-second-order-correction]] sets
$w=-Dh(x)^T(Dh(x)Dh(x)^T)^{-1}h(x+p)$.

[F4] [[thm-sqp-second-order-correction-residual-order]] gives the local
quadratic correction size and cubic active-residual order under its smooth
full-rank hypotheses.

[F5] [[alg-sqp-merit-globalization-with-finite-budgets]] tests the full SOC
candidate against the Armijo threshold.

[A1] $\theta$ is sufficiently small and nonzero, $\rho>0$ is fixed,
$B=I$, the multiplier estimate is $-3/2$, and $\sigma=1/4$.

## Proof

1.1 At $x=(c,s)$, $h(x)=0$, $Dh(x)=2(c,s)$, and $\nabla f(x)=4(c,s)-(1,0)$. The unit tangent $t=(-s,c)$ satisfies $t^T\nabla f(x)=s$. The QP constraint gives $p\in\operatorname{span}(t)$; minimizing $\nabla f(x)^Tp+\tfrac12\|p\|_2^2$ on this line gives $p=-st=(s^2,-sc)$. Its QP multiplier is $-(4-c)/2$, since $p+\nabla f(x)=(4-c)(c,s)$. [given, F1, A1, algebra]

1.2 Here $Dh(x)Dh(x)^T=4$, so [F3] gives $w=(-cs^2/2,-s^3/2)$ and $\|w\|_2=s^2/2$. Direct substitution into the quadratic constraint yields $$h(x+p+w)=\frac{s^4}{4}.$$ The corrected first coordinate is $c+s^2(1-c/2)$, so the corrected objective change is $-s^2(1-c/2)+s^4/2$. Adding the penalty contribution gives $$\psi_\rho(x+p+w)-\psi_\rho(x) =-s^2(1-c/2)+s^4(1/2+\rho/4).$$ [A1, F3, algebra]

2.1 Since $x^Tp=0$ and $\|p\|_2^2=s^2$, $h(x+p)=s^2$. Also $\nabla f(x)^Tp=-s^2$, so [F2] gives $D_\rho=s^2$. The objective changes by $s^2$, while the equality violation changes from zero to $s^2$; hence the full-step merit change is $(1+\rho)s^2>0$, which fails the Armijo right side $-\sigma s^2<0$. [A1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Divide the corrected merit change plus $\sigma D_\rho$ by $s^2$. With $\sigma=1/4$, the result is $-1+c/2+s^2(1/2+\rho/4)+1/4$, which tends to $-1/4$ as $\theta\to0$. It is therefore negative for all sufficiently small nonzero $\theta$, proving the SOC Armijo test passes. The explicit correction also has the $O(s^2)$ norm and $O(s^4)$ residual predicted by [F4]. [A1, F4, F5, step 1.2, algebra] ∎

## Statement

For $f(x,y)=\tfrac12(x^2+y^2)$ subject to $h(x,y)=y=0$, the equality
augmented Lagrangian with penalty $\rho>0$ and multiplier $\nu$ has Hessian
$\operatorname{diag}(1,1+\rho)$. Its exact inner minimizer is
$(0,-\nu/(1+\rho))$, and the multiplier update sends
$\nu$ to $\nu/(1+\rho)$. Thus increasing $\rho$ improves the exact
multiplier contraction factor while worsening the inner Hessian condition
number to $1+\rho$.

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The equality augmented-Lagrangian formula and multiplier update,
with fixed $\rho>0$.

[F1] [[def-sqp-augmented-lagrangian-equality-and-inequality]] defines
$\mathcal L^E_\rho=f+\nu h+\tfrac\rho2h^2$ and
$\nu^+=\nu+\rho h(x^+)$.

[F2] [[alg-sqp-augmented-lagrangian-multiplier-method]] applies that
update after an inner minimization.

[A1] An exact inner routine computes this closed-form minimizer and returns
success within its finite inner cap $M\ge1$; arithmetic is exact and
$\rho>0$.

## Proof

1.1 Substitution into [F1] gives $$\mathcal L^E_\rho(x,y;\nu)=\tfrac12x^2+ \tfrac12(1+\rho)y^2+\nu y.$$ Its Hessian is diagonal with eigenvalues $1$ and $1+\rho$, so the Euclidean spectral condition number is $1+\rho$. [given, A1, F1, algebra]

2.1 The gradient equations are $x=0$ and $(1+\rho)y+\nu=0$; the unique inner minimizer is $(0,-\nu/(1+\rho))$. Its constraint value is $-\nu/(1+\rho)$, so [F1] gives $\nu^+=\nu-\rho\nu/(1+\rho)=\nu/(1+\rho)$. Its absolute contraction factor is $1/(1+\rho)$, which decreases as $\rho$ increases while the condition number in step 1.1 increases. [A1, F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra] ∎

## Definition

The input state is consistent, $(q,p)\in\mathcal M$. For $h=0$, return $(q,p)$ with status `exact-identity`. For nonzero $h$, fix a compact phase subset $C\subset\mathcal M$ over a compact regular configuration chart with $(q,p)\in C$ and $0<|h|<h_0(C)$, using branch balls $U_q,U_p$ supplied by [[lem-rattle-scaled-position-and-momentum-branches]]. The admissible inputs also include initial guesses $\lambda_{\mathrm{init}}\in U_q$, $\mu_{\mathrm{init}}\in U_p$, tolerances $\varepsilon_q,\varepsilon_p\ge0$, finite correction budgets $N_q,N_p\in\mathbb N_0$, and terminating exact factorization/solve backends $\mathcal B_q,\mathcal B_p$ for the two chord calls. Each backend accepts a square $m\times m$ Jacobian, returns a singularity report exactly when it is singular, and otherwise returns a retained factor object. For every right-hand side, solving on this object terminates with the exact unique solution for that matrix; factorization and retained-factor solves are separate operations, as in [[alg-newton-chord-implicit-residual-with-factorization-reuse]]. All evaluations of $c,J,\nabla V$ and the displayed matrix operations in the updates, residual and exact residual-Jacobian evaluations, arithmetic, Euclidean norm evaluation/comparison, and domain-membership tests are returning primitives; no bound on their internal cost is specified. The multiplier domains $U_q,U_p\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ are open balls within the regular branch neighborhoods. Choose the balls so that $F_q$ is $C^1$ on $U_q$ and, for every $\lambda\in U_q$, the corresponding $F_p$ is $C^1$ on $U_p$ and all evaluations in the updates are defined and the corresponding positions remain in the ambient full-row-rank configuration region of the branch lemma. Inconsistent input, missing branch balls, or maps not defined on these domains are outside the algorithm's admissible inputs. On success the routine returns the approximate state, both multipliers, and both scaled residual norms; on failure it returns the residual solver's status, last valid multiplier iterate, and actual scaled residual norm, together with any position-stage values already computed.

1. Form
$$F_q(\lambda)=h^{-2}c\!\left(q+hM^{-1}\left(p-\frac h2\nabla V(q)-hJ(q)^T\lambda\right)\right).$$
Run [[alg-newton-chord-implicit-residual-with-factorization-reuse]] on $F_q$ in chord mode with refresh period $1$, domain $U_q$, initial value $\lambda_{\mathrm{init}}$, tolerance $\varepsilon_q$, budget $N_q$, and backend $\mathcal B_q$. If it returns anything other than `root`, return its exact status (`iteration-budget-exhausted`, `singular-jacobian`, or `invalid-trial`), last valid multiplier iterate, and actual scaled residual norm; do not continue.

2. For its returned $\widetilde\lambda$, compute $\widetilde p_{1/2}=p-\frac h2\nabla V(q)-hJ(q)^T\widetilde\lambda$ and $\widetilde q_1=q+hM^{-1}\widetilde p_{1/2}$. Form
$$F_p(\mu)=h^{-1}J(\widetilde q_1)M^{-1}\left(\widetilde p_{1/2}-\frac h2\nabla V(\widetilde q_1)-hJ(\widetilde q_1)^T\mu\right).$$
Run the same supplier procedure on $F_p$ in chord mode with refresh period $1$, domain $U_p$, initial value $\mu_{\mathrm{init}}$, tolerance $\varepsilon_p$, budget $N_p$, and backend $\mathcal B_p$. If it returns anything other than `root`, return its exact status (`iteration-budget-exhausted`, `singular-jacobian`, or `invalid-trial`), last valid multiplier iterate, actual scaled tangency residual norm, and the successful position-stage values; do not continue.

3. If both calls meet their residual tolerances, set
$$\widetilde p_1=\widetilde p_{1/2}-\frac h2\nabla V(\widetilde q_1)-hJ(\widetilde q_1)^T\widetilde\mu$$
and return $(\widetilde q_1,\widetilde p_1,\widetilde\lambda,\widetilde\mu)$, the norms $\|F_q(\widetilde\lambda)\|_2$, $\|F_p(\widetilde\mu)\|_2$, and status “residual tolerances met”.

For nonzero $h$, leaving a branch ball returns `invalid-trial`, a singular factorization returns `singular-jacobian`, and exhausting either correction budget returns `iteration-budget-exhausted`; the supplier supplies the last valid iterate and its evaluated residual norm in each case. No undefined-evaluation status is needed because the admissible domains require all evaluations to be defined. A successful output with nonzero residuals need not lie in $\mathcal M$; applying the routine again requires a consistent input, for example one restored by [[lem-regular-holonomic-phase-residuals-control-distance-to-phase-manifold]]. The supplier status `root` means only that its stated residual tolerance was met; it does not certify an exact root or a forward-error bound. No finite budget is claimed to succeed on every admissible input.
